vo.text: These are this week's ten trending projects on GitHub.
For each one: what it is, how you use it, and why it helps.
Number ten. Scrapling, a web scraping library for Python.
Fetch a page, pull out the data you want, or crawl a whole website, even from an AI agent.
The benefit: one tool replaces a pile of scrapers, with retries and exports built in.
Number nine. Ziwei Doushu, an open-source engine for a traditional Chinese astrology chart.
Clone it, run the demo, and it draws the full chart for you.
The benefit: builders get the complex rules and a big knowledge base, for free.
Number eight. Hallmark, a design skill that stops AI-built websites from looking AI-built.
Add it to your coding agent, like Claude Code, then ask it to build, redesign or audit a page.
The benefit: original designs, checked in a real browser for contrast and phone layouts.
Number seven, and the most stars this week. T3 Code, a control panel for your coding agents.
Install it, and steer agents like Claude Code and Codex from your desktop, the web, or your phone.
The benefit: one free app for all your agents, even away from your desk.
Number six. OpenMausBot, a chat app where every contact is an AI bot.
Each bot runs Claude or Codex on your machine, with its own personality, model and cloud computer.
The benefit: a team of assistants you can watch at work, approving only what matters.
Number five. Claude Code Game Studios turns one Claude session into a game studio.
Clone it, type /start, and 49 specialised agents, from directors to testers, guide your project.
The benefit: you make every decision, while the team keeps the game organised and catches mistakes.
Number four. Anthropic Skills, the public library of Agent Skills for Claude.
A skill is a folder of instructions and scripts that Claude loads when a task needs it.
The benefit: repeatable results, like documents in your brand style, every time.
Number three. Worktrunk, a command-line tool for git worktrees.
One command, wt switch, gives each AI agent its own working copy of your code.
The benefit: run many agents in parallel, without them stepping on each other.
Number two. Claude Mem gives your coding agent a memory.
Install it with one command. It takes notes while your agent works, and brings them back next session.
The benefit: no more explaining your project from scratch every time.
And number one. NVIDIA Auto Ontology.
It reads your data's metadata and builds a map of what every table and metric means, for AI agents.
The benefit: agents write correct queries, and every answer shows where it came from.
That's this week on GitHub. Pick one, and try it this weekend.
